text:
Jordan B.: Heads-up — saw an SDK vs REST parity issue around streaming chat + function calls while testing the sample-app. REST streaming sends chunked function_call payloads and finish_reason semantics, but the Node SDK conflates the chunks and exposes a different param name for requesting function calls. Breaks our code that auto-invokes tools.

Jordan B.: REST streaming repro (works):

curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream -d '{"model":"chat-3","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"call weather(\"\"NYC\"\")"}],"function_call":"auto"}'

This yields chunked events where function_call begins as {"name":"getWeather"} then later chunks append args as separate data events, and final event has finish_reason: "function_call".

Jordan B.: Node SDK attempt (fails / wrong shape):

// @redwood/sdk v0.10.0
const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
const stream = await c.chat.stream({ model: 'chat-3', messages, functionCalling: 'auto' });
// SDK emits a single `function_call` event with args concatenated incorrectly like: "{\"temp\": 70true}" and never surfaces finish_reason reliably. Also note param name `functionCalling` vs REST `function_call`.

Priya S.: Oof. Looks like two problems: (A) naming/param drift (camelCase in SDK vs snake_case in REST) which we usually translate in the transport layer but apparently missed for the streaming/func-call path; (B) streaming event handling — SDK's incremental parser is reassembling chunks naively and losing separators, causing invalid JSON args.

Stream Bot: stream/sanitizer: dropped malformed chunk at 1802000204, parse error at offset 128

Alex G.: Also saw different retry behavior when the stream closed with a 503 transient. Direct REST callers reconnect after honoring Retry-After; SDK's stream helper auto-reconnects immediately and replays the original request, causing duplicate tool invocations. For function_call flows that call external systems, that's bad.

Jordan B.: Short-term workaround: fall back to raw fetch/websocket to the streaming endpoint and implement our own chunk parser and retry handling. Sample-app onboarding flow switched to raw streaming and works.

Priya S.: Plan: (1) add a proper `function_call` named option to SDK method signatures (alias old camelCase but keep snake_case mapping at transport); (2) fix the incremental chunk parser to preserve chunk boundaries and reconstruct function_call args safely (emit partialArg events); (3) change stream retry behavior to honor Retry-After and expose an `onRetry`/`shouldRetry` callback so apps can avoid re-invoking side-effecting function calls; (4) add e2e that simulates chunked function_call args and a transient 503 during stream to assert no duplicate calls.

Alex G.: I'll own the parser and the retry change for Node. Priya — can you coordinate API/typing changes so Python and Go match? We need cross-language parity.

CI Bot: integration/tests/streaming_function_call -> FAILED at 1802000300 (parser produced invalid JSON)

Jordan B.: Filed issue redwood/sdk#1402 with traces and sample-app links; marked sample-app onboarding as blocked by sdk parity.

Priya S.: We'll add a migration note: SDK now accepts both `function_call` and `functionCalling` for a release cycle, then deprecate camelCase. Also documenting the retry-change since it affects idempotency.

Alex G.: I'll PR a patch with tests and ping @eng-runtime to validate chunk format from the service; want to ensure server delimiting isn't ambiguous.

Jordan B.: Thanks — keeping sample-app on raw streaming for now. Once SDK lands I'll switch back. :thumbsup:
